title: Last call
logline: Friday. Last call through the wall. The bar's lights going off, drawn as the plaster going dark. Then one sound: the back door. Then the alley: one regular, from behind, walking home past the garage. The only one the strip ever draws outside the wall.

panels.composition: The garage, late. The wall: the shapes going dim. LAST CALL as a shape of sound in the plaster.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a garage wall where figures drawn in the plaster are fading as a bar closes behind it, no words

panels.composition: The wall, dark. One sound: a door. Drawn as a small rectangle of light in the plaster, then gone.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a dark plaster wall with one small rectangle of light where a door opens and closes, no words

panels.composition: The alley through the garage's window. One REGULAR, from behind, in a hat, walking home. Slow. Real, for once, outside the wall.

characters.pose: one, from behind, in a hat

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, seen through a garage window, a man in a hat walking slowly away down an alley at night, no words
image.notes: The only regular the strip draws outside the plaster. From behind. The hat.

panels.composition: WOOD at the window. BARNABY. The alley empty. The tavern dark. The wall a wall. The strip doesn't name the man or the bar.

image.prompt: brush-pen line with muddy early-digital flats, a man and a dog at a garage window looking at an empty alley beside a dark tavern, no words

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind

notes: Last call in the plaster. One regular, from behind, outside the wall.
